name: Kaniet-Dempwolff
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beiträge zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. MSOS 8 (contains his Kaniet material; not found online; per Glottolog kani1283).

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1996. The linguistic position of the Western Islands, Papua New Guinea. In John Lynch & Fa'afo Pat (eds), Oceanic studies: proceedings of the First International Conference on Oceanic Linguistics, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics C-133.
sources.note: Section 3.3 and pp. 29-31 give a phonemic interpretation of Dempwolff's Kaniet (Table 18: 19 consonants, 5 vowels) from the 1905 orthography; segments only, nothing on stress for either Kaniet list. (Stress is discussed at length only for Wuvulu-Aua, from Blust's own 1975 fieldwork.) Confirms Thilenius 1903 and Dempwolff 1905 are the only data on Kaniet and that the two lists are different languages.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kani1283 (comment citing Blust 1996:40 on the two mutually unintelligible Kaniet languages; refs Dempwolff 1905).

Smythe, W.E. 1970. Melanesian, Micronesian, and Indonesian features in languages of the Admiralty Islands. In S.A. Wurm & D.C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1209-1234. Pacific Linguistics C-13.
sources.note: Nothing; Kaniet appears only in feature counts, with fn. 9 (p. 1231): 'The figures for Kaniet are not very reliable owing to the big discrepancy between Thilenius' and my word lists.'

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beiträge zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen 8 (Abt. 1): 182-254; section d) 'Kanied (Anachoreten)', pp. 205-208; introduction p. 182.
sources.note: Kanied section (pp. 205-208) is a bare wordlist + 'Verbalformen', place and personal names, with NO prose remark on stress (unlike section c) Agomes p. 201, which says 'Die Betonung findet fast ausnahmslos auf der letzten Silbe statt'). Only the article-wide convention on p. 182: 'Die Betonung pflegte ich oft nicht zu bezeichnen, wenn sie der uns geläufigen auf der vorletzten Silbe entsprach.' Individual Kanied forms carry sporadic acute accents in mixed positions: penult (uáfu, tóhu, fáfu, tásin, lepónu, sénano, kekéu, páfi, úba, haféfin), antepenult (hímiab, hímisen, támisän, χéalo), final…

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1976. Austronesian languages: Admiralty Islands area. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 349-364. Pacific Linguistics C-39.

sources.citation: Smythe, W.E. n.d. Unpublished Kaniet field material (referred to in Smythe 1970:1231 fn. 9 and Blust 1996:27), probably collected from Kaniet descendants on Allison Island, Ninigo lagoon; with Smythe, W.E. n.d. Seimat grammar and vocabulary, MS (78 pp.).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only post-1905 Kaniet data ever collected; if from the Allison-Island Kaniet community it may represent Dempwolff's variety rather than Thilenius's and could contain stress marking or remarks. Whereabouts unknown (possibly SIL-PNG Ukarumpa or ANU/Pacific Linguistics archives).

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1904. Über aussterbende Völker. (Die Eingeborenen der 'westlichen Inseln' in Deutsch-Neu-Guinea.) Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 36: 384-415.

sources.note: Dempwolff's ethnographic report on the same Dec 1902 visit to the Kaniet/Anchorite Islands; the only other first-hand publication by the sole recorder of this variety. Almost certainly no phonology, but the one unchecked Dempwolff item; ZfE 36 should be public-domain on archive.

sources.citation: Thilenius, Georg. 1903. Ethnographische Ergebnisse aus Melanesien, II: Die westlichen Inseln des Bismarck-Archipels. Nova Acta, Abhandlungen der Kaiserl. Leop.-Carol. Deutschen Akademie der Naturforscher 80(2): 103-406. Halle. (Kaniet vocabulary, 296 words.)

sources.note: The other Kaniet list; per Blust 1996 a different language (Glottolog kani1245), so it cannot supply a kani1283 statement, but any stress remark there is the nearest sister-language evidence and is needed for the kani1245 entry anyway. Public domain; likely on archive.org/BHL.
